context: The user supplied several centralized-exchange interface references and requested that XRBitcoinCash pages adopt a denser professional exchange/workbench layout, starting with the Liquidity Pool, while preserving existing JavaScript and using the existing shared project CSS efficiently.

canonical_visual_layer.rule: Do not globally apply the exchange shell to unreviewed pages.

design_direction.reference: Modern centralized-exchange/workbench information architecture without copying third-party branding or content.
design_direction.palette: Neutral black/charcoal surfaces, thin neutral borders, blue primary actions, green/red only for meaningful positive/negative state, amber for attention/security.
design_direction.density: Compact cards, rows, tables, segmented controls and progressive disclosure rather than long stacked decorative sections.
design_direction.navigation: Desktop fixed navigation rail where useful; responsive compact top navigation on smaller screens.
design_direction.action_layout: Primary work surface with a secondary account/wallet/action rail where the page purpose benefits from it.
design_direction.motion: Motion must communicate functional state. Avoid decorative scan lines, ambient green/red lines, or unnecessary grid animation in normal exchange workspaces.
design_direction.imagery: Prefer existing project/token images and CSS-native icons. Decorative imagery must not displace functional data.
design_direction.beginner_ux: Keep the primary action path plain-language and visually prominent; technical/raw evidence remains available but secondary.

migration_method: Fetch the current source-of-truth head and inspect the target page before editing.
Use public/xrbc-dynamic-ui.css as the shared visual system when the page already loads it.
Opt the page in with body/layout classes rather than duplicating a large page-local redesign stylesheet.
Preserve existing IDs, data attributes, names, form controls, event targets, script order and script contents for a visual-only task.
Prefer CSS and native HTML details/summary/tab/button-group disclosure before adding JavaScript.
Version the shared CSS URL on the migrated page for cache invalidation.
For CSS-only migrations, compare every executable script block before and after and require byte-identical scripts.
Check duplicate HTML IDs and run runtime-contract CI.
Browser-review desktop and mobile rendering before treating the page as the reference for the next migration.
Migrate one page at a time; do not perform a one-shot repository-wide markup rewrite.

presentation_changes: Desktop navigation becomes a fixed left rail; smaller screens collapse to compact top navigation.
Liquidity Manager remains the primary work area and Xaman remains the secondary account/action rail.
Action modes use a compact segmented control with a high-contrast selected state.
Normal primary actions are blue rather than decorative green/red.
Pool metrics become dense neutral market cards.
Decorative green chart scan/grid effects are disabled under the exchange shell.
Wallet/LP details and technical sections stay available as secondary information.

intentionally_unchanged: XRPL signing, submission and validated-finality checks
pending: Visually verify the deployed Liquidity Pool on desktop and mobile.
Adjust only presentation/density issues discovered during browser review; keep JavaScript unchanged unless a separate functional request requires it.
After the Liquidity Pool design is accepted, migrate the next page using the same opt-in shared CSS method.
